activity.notes: Cadwallon ap Cadfan is unusually well attested for a seventh-century Welsh king and succeeded his father in Gwynedd around 625. He allied with Penda, defeated Edwin of Northumbria, and died at Heavenfield. Bede's calendrical reckoning leaves a genuine 633-versus-634 debate for his death, so both ends are retained at approximate year-level rather than overstated as exact.

sources.title: Cadwallon ap Cadfan — historical summary
sources.citation_text: The summary gives Cadwallon's reign in Gwynedd as c.625-634 and discusses the 633/634 chronological dispute over his death.

sources.title: Canu Cadwallon — historical background
sources.citation_text: The historical background notes that Cadwallon is very well attested by seventh-century Welsh standards, with Bede, Adomnan, annalistic and genealogical evidence.
